original_value: AbstractArtificial intelligence and deep learning methods hold great promise in the medical sciences in areas such as enhanced tumor identification from radiographic images, and natural language processing to extract complex information from electronic health records. Scientific review of AI algorithms has involved reproducibility, in which investigators share protocols, raw data, and programming codes. Within the realm of medicine, reproducibility introduces important challenges, including risk to patient privacy, challenges in reproducing results, and questions regarding ownership and financial value of large medical datasets. Scientific review, however, mandates some form of resolution of these inherent conflicts. We propose several approaches to permit scientific review while maintaining patient privacy and data confidentiality.

result.paraphrase: AbstractArtificial intelligence and deep learning hold considerable promise in medicine, including improved tumor detection in radiographic images and natural language processing for extracting complex information from electronic health records. The scientific assessment of AI algorithms has centered on reproducibility, where investigators share protocols, raw data, and programming code. In medicine, reproducibility creates significant challenges, such as patient privacy risks, difficulty replicating results, and concerns about the ownership and financial worth of large medical datasets. Nonetheless, scientific review requires some means of resolving these built-in conflicts. We propose several methods to enable scientific review while preserving patient privacy and data confidentiality.
